cells.remarks: States that Rēvaṇa took the oath in the presence of the representatives of the twelve liṅgas, the sixteen of the eight groups, and five-hundred of Ayyāvoḷe to kill Saṁmanāka who had killed Mañgaja and that he fulfilled the same by entering the village when Saṁmanāka was eating and drinking the blood of the murderer. In the course of this vendetta he is also stated to have killed twelve persons including two babies in the cradle. An assembly of the above mentioned bodies gave Rēvaṇa the title 'poyeyabeṇkoḷva' and exempted him from the payment of certain taxes. Published in Karnataka Inscriptions, Vol. IV, pp. 119 ff.

The gift was made for the merit of the king on the occasion of a lunar eclipse. The land seems to have been entrusted to the care of Bhōgun Chennayya and Pānayya, who were themselves the recipients of another gift of 4 tūmu of land for their own maintenance. Cf. Nos. 1, 3 and 5 above.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri — Telangana

cells.remarks: States that Rēchervula Nāmiredđi, son of Kāma, had three lingas, Kāmēšvara, Kāchēšvara and Nāmēšvara, installed at trikūṭa in Pillalamarri after the names of his parents and after his own name for their merit as well as his own and made a gift of 7 marturu of wet land behind Sabbi-samudram besides 7 maṭtu of dry land for worship and offerings to the deities. Also records a gift of land near Viśvanātĵasamudram to god Nāmēšvara and further lands under Kuđukudiya-Gaura-samudram for the maintenance of the gardens of the temple. Published in Hyderabad Archaeological Series, No. 13, Inscription No. 38.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana
cells.place: Same pillar, three other faces
cells.date: Śaka 1124 (anāudhi-nētra-rudra), Dun-dubhi, Chaitra śu. 14, Saturday=1202 A.D., March 9.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Rēcherla family to which Nāma (Nāmi-reḍḍi) belonged and states that he had filled the god Viśvanāthēśvara temple with ornaments, gift of the two tanks called Guṇḍacheruvu and Kaṭavācheruvu and lands under them as vritti; Aitami, wife of Nāma and Viśvanātha, their son, installed the deities Aitēśvara and Viśvanāthēśvara respectively and made endowments of lands for the same. He registered the gift of land to Prolēśvara by Vallasi-ni, the sister of Viśvanātha who had the deity installed in the name of her son Prōla. Ibid., No. 41.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana
cells.place: Slab to the left of entrance to the inner maṇḍapa of Nāmēśvara shrine in the same temple.
cells.remarks: States that Recheruvula Nāmī-reddi endowed houses in the fort of Pillalamarri to several servants of the temple of Ānamēśvara. The chief bears several epithets like temple-kāmaṇi-puravarēśvara, Bōlavandaṁda and Manumamukāditya. In characters of about the 12th century. Ibid., No. 37.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana
cells.place: Four-faced pillar set up on a platform by the side of Peddagudi. First two faces.
cells.date: Saka 1130 (suravartma-Rāma-šasabhřid-višvam̂bharā), Vibhava, Jyēshtha šu. 3 (Mřidānyā-tīthi), Monday=1208 A.D., May 19.
cells.remarks: States that Erapāṁbā, wife of Pillalamarri Bēti-reddi of the Recherla family had the deity Erakkēśvara (named after her) installed in the village Pillalamarri and endowed lands under the tank Erakasamudra, which she had bought, constructed by her in the village Pillalamarri, for worship, offerings, repairs,etc. in the temple and for maintaining the members of the establishment and the maṭha attached to it; further gifts of land were made to the same temple by Erapāṁbā and her husband Kāmasēvāra and Erakkēśvara installed by her and named after her parents; also records grants for a temple (?) constructed by her brother Nūṁka-nāyaka. The genealogical accounts of both Erapāṁbā and her husband Bēti-reddi are given in the beginning. Ibid., no. 42.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana
cells.place: Third face of the same pillar
cells.date: Saka 1137, Yuva, Māgha ba. 15, Friday, solar eclipse=1216 A.D., February 19.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the above. Registers the gift of all waste-land under Erāka-samudram, excluding those given away as vrittis, to the gods and Brāhmanas, as also all the garden-lands thereat to god Erākēsvara probably by Errapāmbā; further gifts of lands to the deities Erākēsvaradēva and Mūlasthāna-Māchidēva set up on the tank-bund of Erākasamudra, and to the deities Bētēsvara and Erākēsvara installed by Imatūri Sōmayya, are registered. A postscript registers gifts of lands under Lakuma-samudram and Erāka-samudram to god Komarēsvara. Ibid., No. 42.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana

cells.remarks: Registers the gifts of land under Eraka-samudra for maintaining a satra, a cook-house, feeding alms-houses for students and poor, etc. engraved. This is engraved in continuation of No. 222 above. In characters of the 13th century. Ibid., No. 39.

cells.location: NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK · NALGONDA DISTRICT SURYAPET TALUK Pillalamarri † — Telangana
cells.place: Below No. 223 above

cells.remarks: States that the image of the deity Erakēśvara, which was damaged by Sultān Allavādin during the disturbances of that period, was reinstalled by Erapotu-lanka who also made a gift of land behind the Dēvarakuṇṭa at Pillalamarri for offerings to the deity. The donor, who was ruling over Pillalamarri, was a servant of Kāpaya-nāyaka, son of Kipaya-bhēta like Āṁdhrarāśēkhivaram, Anumakondigaṁtpavaravādhīśvara, Chidōrarāśāthapānāchārya, Kāmēśvarakāpāluka, etc. Ibid., No. 40.

cells.location: Ghōshārvā, Patna District, Bihar. — Bihar

cells.remarks: Records the construction of a building for the Vajrāsana by Viradēva who hailed from Nagarahāra and who was the son of the Brāhmaṇa Indragupta. He is also stated to have built two chaityas on the hill Indraśaila. Gives a detailed account of his deep study of the Vēdas, his becoming a Buddhist monk ultimately heading the Nalanda monastery, his visit to the Kanishka-vihāra and Vajrāsana and his influence over the king Dēvapāla. In characters of about the 10th century. Published in JASB, Vol. XVII, pt. 1, pp. 492-501; Ind. Ant., Vol. XVII, pp. 307-312; and Gauḍalēkha-mālā, pp. 45-54 and Plate.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH · Dēopāđā. Rajshahi District, East Pakistan. — Andhra Pradesh

cells.remarks: Records the building of a temple of Pradyumnēśvara by the king whose genealogy and eulogy are given. The king is said to have defeated Nānya, Vīra and the kings of Gauḍa, Kāmarūpa and Kaliṅga, imprisoned Rāgha, Vardhana and Vīra; led a naval expedition along the course of the Ganges. The composer and the engraver of the inscription were Umāpatidhara and Rāṇaka Śūlapāṇi respectively. Published in JASB, Vol. XXXIV, Pt. 1, pp. 128-54; Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 305-15 and Plate; and Inscriptions of Bengal, Vol. III, pp. 42-56 and Plate.

cells.location: Bōdh Gayā, Gaya District, Bihar. — Bihar

cells.location: Bōdh Gayā, Gaya District, Bihar. † — Bihar

His guru paramparā is also given. Published in CII, Vol. III, pp. 274-278, Pl.XI-A. See also Ind. Ant., Vol. XX, p. 190 and Bhandarkar's List, No. 1325.

cells.location: Eraṇ, Sagar District, Madhya Pradesh. — Madhya Pradesh

cells.remarks: States that Hariyāṇa-sūri (or Harihara-sūri), pupil of Siṁhanandyāchārya, who was himself a pupil of Vidyāṇandasvāmi, died on the second date and that the memorial slab (niśidhi) was set up by him. Records the gifts of the village Vāgaṇāḍu and Akshaya made on the first and the third dates respectively to the Nēminātha-basti at Bandavaḍa. The gifts were entrusted to Muniyanna, pupil of Siṁhanandyāchārya and were to be administered by his sons and grandsons. It is stated that at the time, Sōma, son of Laṇdā, was governing Gōvē. An endorsement at the end of the record states that the place Bandavādi was established by a king named Śrīpāla in early days and Virugapa, son of Maṁgadaṇḍa, built the temple of Nēminīrtha, and that the latter was renovated at the instance of Simhanandi.

cells.remarks: . Begins with the prāsasti, Pūmalar tiruvum, etc., of the king. Records a royal order issued from the seat Maļavarāyaṇ, at the instance of [Maļa ?]varāyar limiting to 2 achchu, the total amount of various taxes, such as kađamai, antarāyam etc., payable on various pieces of land, bought of Tirukkōdīkā-udaiyān Tirukkađambamarndān alias Koṅgarāyaṇ of Pūmbi-jāl in Kāñai-irukkai, the kilāṇ of Variśjiyūr and various others and gifted as the maintenance (jīvitam) of the servants engaged in the tiruchchiṇnam service for god Tiruvālavāyu-dāiya-nāyaṇār of Madurai in Māđakkuļakkīl, instituted by Oruvāruṇarndān Enakku-nalla-Perumāļ alias Anṇan Tami-la-pPallavaraiyar of Rājavallabhapuram in Kiļ-Vēmba-nādu. One of the lamps was gifted by a certain Senthālaiarai Protkalan-Uḍaiyān of Tiruvadavūr in Ten-parappu-nāḍu and the other by Maṇikkanār. Both these lots of sheep were entrusted in equal lots to three cowherds (surabhi-dāyin) of the temple who agreed to supply ghee for the lamps.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu

cells.remarks: Records the royal order at the instance of Teṇṇagaddēvīran, exempting the lands granted to the temple of Tirumarai-nāyanār by different individuals from payment of taxes and arranging for the payment of the levies antarāyam, kaḍamai and kuḍimai on these lands to the temple treasury. The grant was to take effect from the 5+1st year. In characters of about the 13th century. Cf. No. 471 above.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .
cells.remarks: Damaged and partly erased. Seems to record a grant of land as dēvadāna of the god, made tax-free from the month of Āpī of the [2] 9th regnal year of the king. Refers to a royal order in earlier years restricting the sale of villages such as Tuvarattūr, Mēlappallikkurichchi, Puliñgurinchi etc. Details are lost. In characters of the 13th century.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .
cells.remarks: Seems to be a royal order prohibiting the collection of ponpari on the lands granted to the temple. Quotes some year in the reign of Sundarapāṇḍya. Do.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .
cells.remarks: Records the royal order granting the village Sirukulam in Kaḷa-vaḷi-nāḍu as dēvadāna to god Tirumarai-nāyanār and stipulating that the land (urai) and the kuṟi (i.e. the village) may continue to rest with Pāṇan Aiyyanāyan and that the levies kaḍamai, etc. from the village amounting to one achchu might be paid into the temple treasury with effect from the month Ani of the 34th year for offerings to the god. Do.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .
cells.remarks: Records the undertaking given to the same temple as mentioned in No. 476 above by the ūrār of Kāḷatēri in Teṇ- Kaḷavali-nāḍu in respect of the assignment of income from levies from Sirukulam in favour of the temple following the order of Ulaguḍaiya-nāyanār. Mentions the pampat- Perumāḷ alias Divākaran. (Cf. No. 492 below). Do.

cells.location: MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · MELUR TALUK Tiruvādavūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall .
cells.remarks: Records of 'royal order addressed to the paḍakkāravaṇar of Pallikkurichchi informing them that after their village to the temple of the god mentioned in No. 476 above as dēvadāna and directing them to pay the poṇvari of ten achchu to the temple, Do.

Probably the income from the levies on the land was to be utilised for burning lamps before some deities one of which is stated to have been set up by the above person, and Aṉiyāṅkādēvar. Refers to the flooding of the dēvadāna lands due to breaches in tanks. Cf. Nos. 494 and 495 below.

cells.location: MADRAS / MADURAI DISTRICT / MELUR TALUK · Tiruvādāvūr—contd. / Melur taluk—contd. † — Tamil Nadu

It is stated that the land had lain fallow due to the silting up of the tank and refers to the non-payment of the poṉvari. As a consequence, Śrīvallabha Vilupparaiyar is mentioned in this connection. Rājagōpāla is also mentioned. Cf. Nos. 485, 493 and 494 above.

cells.remarks: Damaged and top portion lost. States that the king's preceptor Rudrasarman, having received the village Hulichuru in Bhalunike-86, a kampana of Mēlāpalli as dakshiṇā from the king when the latter performed several kratas in his name at Ghaṭṭaikā-Bīrahalli, and having made the same through a royal charter a free gift to god Rudrasarman, assisted by him at agrahāra Gōnante for worship, offerings and other services in the temple and feeding and clothing the ascetics, teachers and students therein. Further gifts of land-income from taxes like tippe-sunka and an oil-mill are registered. Besides the brahmadaas mentioned, the king were temple servants received one house-site. The early part of the record gives an account of the family of this preceptor of Vasiṣṭha-vamśa who is said to have been born of Govardhana-bhaṭṭa and Araikabbe by the grace of god Kumbhēśvara of Bāgevāḍi.

cells.place: Rafijõle-Khēgi—Slab kept behind the Hanumān temple.
cells.remarks: Broken into three pieces and badly worn out. Registers gifts of lands and money to gods Hemmēsvara and Mallikārjuna of Reṇjēru by mahamaṇḍalēśvara Bhairavadeva of the Sinda family whose genealogical account is given in detail. The gift was made into the hands of Varēvaradeva who was the sthānapati of the temple of Farēśvara and a disciple by the mahājanas and other individuals to the deity Hemmēsvara, and to the Brāhmaṇas of the Brahmapurī of that god and also to Bhāskara who wrote the record are enumerated. Reṇjēru is said to have been situated in Aṭṭale-nāḍu and givas also a genealogy with him of his four sons of Nidulūḍi-Sinda, the progenitor of the family. The other three sons, viz., Satyasārya, Prabhusēvya and Budhasēvya, are stated to have been ruling over Paliyāṁda-maṇḍala, Bigadage-dēśa and Balljāre-nāḍu respectively.

Also mentions Jagadēkamalla's subordinate Bammanayya, his wife Lakkhādēvi and their son Hemmādēvara. Records the renovation of the temple of god Bālēśvara, originally built by Bāli-sēṭṭi, by Bhāskara-sēṭṭi and the completion of the temple of Kēdāreśvara and another temple by Kēṭi-sēṭṭi, by Sāgara-sēṭṭi in the sarvamānzeya-agrahāra Śāleyasīmala, situated in Gonka-nāḍu, a sub-division of Ālande-1000 in Kuntala-janapada. Further records that Gorikarasa, the ruler of Gonka-nāḍu, Nagayya, the prabhu of the village, purahitas and vaidyas Kēṭi-sēṭṭi together granted 2 māṇa of flower-garden to the deity Bālēśvara for worship in and repairs to the temple, etc. The record enjoins Bammanayya, Lakkhidēvi and Hemmāḍi-dēvarasa, among others, to protect the grant.

Gives the genealogical list of a Jain family beginning with Jala, Jaskara, and ending with Bhimasiha in Chittrakūṭa (i.e. Chittorgarh). Composed by Śubhākīrti and engraved by Sūdra. In characters of about the 12th century. Cf. PIRASWC, 1904-05, No. 2202.

cells.remarks: . The first part, composed by Śrīnivāsa, son of Sthirānanda, records that the queen Nōhalā, the wife of Kēyūravarsha, erected a temple of Śiva and donated to it a number of villages. The second part, composed by Sajjana, son of Thīra, records that Lakshmanarāja (II), the son of Yuvarājadēva (I) and Nōhalā, made over the monastery of the holy Vaidyanātha also called Nauhalēśvara to the Śaiva ascetic Hiridayaśiva who placed it in the charge of his disciple Aghōraśiva. The third part which was composed by the Kāyastha Siruka records the payment of taxes by the traders for the benefit of the monastery. The praśasti is stated to have deserved praise from the famous poet Rājaśekhara. It was written by Nāi, son of the karaṇika Dhīra and was engraved by Nōnna, son of the Sūtradhāra Saṅgama.
